evals.prompt: Hey, I'm working on a Node.js Express API and I keep noticing we have like 4 or 5 different places where we validate email addresses — each one is slightly different. Some use a regex, one uses a library. Can you do a tech debt audit on the src/validators directory and consolidate everything?
evals.expected_output: The skill explores the validators directory, identifies all duplicated email validation implementations, explains which differ and how, proposes a single canonical implementation, replaces all callsites, and deletes the duplicates. Ends with a summary of what was changed.
expectations: The response identifies multiple duplicate email validation implementations across different files
The response checks whether the duplicates have diverged (i.e., behave differently from each other)
The response identifies or proposes a canonical implementation to consolidate around
The response shows or describes the before/after of the consolidation
The response replaces or describes replacing callsites with the canonical version before deleting duplicates
The response ends with a cleanup summary listing what was deleted/consolidated

evals.prompt: Our repo has gotten pretty messy. We haven't cleaned it up in like 6 months and there's a lot of dead code — old feature flags that were supposed to be temporary, commented-out functions, exports that nothing uses anymore. Can you do a full dead code sweep on the src/ folder?
evals.expected_output: The skill scans for unused exports, unreachable branches tied to stale flags, commented-out code blocks, and unread variables. It groups findings by risk/confidence, presents them to the user, then removes confirmed dead code with explanations for any that were flagged but not deleted.
expectations: The response identifies multiple categories of dead code (unused exports, stale feature flags, commented-out blocks)
The response groups or prioritizes findings by confidence or risk before removing anything
The response mentions verifying code is truly unreachable before deleting (dynamic imports, string-based lookups)
The response identifies stale feature flags by name and proposes their removal
The response does not silently delete code — explains what was removed and why
The response ends with a summary of what was deleted and what was flagged but left for the user to decide

evals.prompt: I'm about to start a new sprint and want to pay down some tech debt first. We have a Python Django project. I don't know exactly where to start — can you do a general tech debt audit and give me a prioritized list of what to tackle?
evals.expected_output: The skill scopes the audit to the whole project, explores for all debt categories (duplication, dead code, complexity, inconsistent patterns, magic values), produces a categorized and prioritized inventory with severity indicators, and asks the user which items they want to address first.
expectations: The response covers at least 4 of the 7 debt categories (duplication, dead code, god objects, deep nesting, magic values, inconsistent patterns, overly complex functions)
The response uses severity indicators or priority ordering (e.g., critical/moderate/minor or high/medium/low)
The response organizes findings by category, not as a flat unstructured list
The response does not immediately start making edits — it presents the inventory first and checks with the user
God objects or large structural issues are flagged but not immediately extracted inline
The response asks the user which items to tackle first or offers a recommended starting point
